_comment: Each garment SVG is generated independently, so it never shares the body's exact framing/scale. transform (scale, tx, ty) is calibrated once per asset by matching the garment's own figure bounding box (full height, horizontal center) against the base body's bounding box in body-solo-front.svg (canvas 1333x2000). Apply as: transform="translate(tx,ty) scale(scale)" on a <g> wrapping the garment's inner paths, layered on top of the body. IMPORTANT: the raw vectorization of a garment reference image contains the WHOLE figure (skin, head, everything from that source image), not just the garment shape — stacking it raw repaints the body underneath with that image's own skin tone. Every garment file here has already been stripped down to only its garment-colored paths (skin-tone and background paths removed by color-distance matching against body-solo-front.svg's palette) so it layers transparently everywhere except the actual garment.
_rasterComment: Raster garments (photorealistic renders, generated isolated/no-model with the reference body's proportions in mind) are placed directly in body SVG units via `rect` {x,y,width,height} — the whole PNG canvas is drawn at that rect with an <image> element, no per-path transform needed. `rect` was calibrated once per garment by overlaying the PNG on body-solo-front.svg and eyeballing shoulder/torso fit; every color variant shares the same rect since they're color-only edits of the same base render (identical framing/dimensions). Colors are a fixed set of pre-rendered images (via Adobe HSL colorize + background removal), not a live recolor — add a new color by running the same recolor+cutout pass on the base image and adding a file entry.
